sources.citation: Allen Hatcher, Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology, author-hosted Cornell draft, 1980s with minor revisions 1999/2000.
source_limitations: Unfinished draft; author says much remains to be done.
Seifert classification for base S² with three multiple fibres is explicitly not proved; exercises/omitted cases remain.

sources.citation: William Thurston, The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds, 1980 Princeton-distributed lecture notes, electronic edition 1.1, March 2002.
sources.read_scope: All pages of complete PDF chapter files 1-9 and 11; 312 PDF pages. This is not a full-book read. Chapters 10 and 12 are absent in this edition; other chapters not read.
source_limitations: Archive explicitly says these are the 1980 notes typed in TeX without content updates (2002 edition).
Several proofs are sketches or depend on cited results.
Chapter 9 is incomplete in this edition; tameness/strong-convergence statements are conditional or historical.

sources.citation: Joel Hass, Jeffrey C. Lagarias, Nicholas Pippenger, The Computational Complexity of Knot and Link Problems, JACM 46 (1999), 185-211; author-hosted reprint.
sources.result_contract: For an n-crossing diagram, Haken's finite normal-coordinate search decides whether it is a knot diagram for the unknot in O(exp(c n²)) Turing time and O(n² log n) space; the Jaco-Tollefson vertex-surface search takes O(exp(c' n)) time and the same space. The input decision also rejects diagrams that are not knot diagrams. Theorem 1.1 supplies a polynomial certificate, hence unknot recognition is in NP.
source_limitations: Theorem 5.4 cites Haken/Schubert/Jaco-Rubinstein/Jaco-Oertel/Jaco-Tollefson instead of proving normal-surface existence.
Theorem 5.6 is referred to a Jaco-Tollefson corollary.
Lemma 4.1 essential-disk/unknot equivalence is only sketched.
Not a self-contained complete proof source for the deep algorithmic ingredients.

sources.citation: Léo Bénard, Vincent Florens, Adrien Rodau, A slope invariant and the A-polynomial of knots, New York Journal of Mathematics 30 (2024), 561-582.
key_locators: Theorem 5.2, ideal point and boundary slope
sources.result_contract: With the paper's variable order A=A_K(L,M), for an irreducible character component X whose peripheral restriction image has dimension one, s_K(χ)=-(M/L)(∂_M A/∂_L A) as a rational identity where defined. At an ideal point on a one-dimensional A-polynomial component, the slope is minus the corresponding Culler-Shalen boundary slope / Newton-polygon edge slope, with the paper's stated peripheral convention.
source_limitations: Slope function is only defined on relevant admissible loci / boundary-parabolic treatment; not every character.
Requires dimension-one restriction image for Theorem 4.1.
Imports Culler-Shalen surfaces and torsion facts.

sources.citation: John A. Baldwin, Steven Sivek, Torus knots, the A-polynomial, and SL(2,C), arXiv:2405.19197v2, 28 Nov 2025 accepted preprint, 22 pages; published Mathematische Annalen 394 (2026), online 13 Feb 2026, pp. 1-26, DOI 10.1007/s00208-026-03363-2.
sources.read_pages: 1-22 complete for the accepted arXiv v2; publisher version not separately read
result_contract: A knot in S3 has infinitely many rational SL(2,C)-abelian surgeries iff it is a torus knot.
The enhanced A-polynomial Newton polygon is contained in a line iff the knot is a torus knot.
Enhanced-A-polynomial detection and its Alexander-degree strengthening classify specified torus knots as stated in Corollaries 1.3-1.4.
For nontrivial fibered non-torus knots with exactly two boundary slopes, Theorem 1.7 gives a slope-zero separating incompressible surface or at least three slopes.
source_limitations: Proof depends on instanton Floer/L-space results and imported A-polynomial/Culler-Shalen literature.
Ordinary A-polynomial torus detection and the two-slope characterization remain open questions in the paper.
Results stated for knots in S3; general 3-manifolds are posed as a question.

exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.locator: Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology, §1.2, Theorem 1.9; statement PDF p. 15 / printed p. 14; proof uniqueness PDF pp. 22-24 / printed pp. 21-23.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.claim: Disjoint incompressible tori cut into atoroidal or Seifert-fibered pieces; minimal collection is unique up to isotopy.
proof_ingredients: Triangulation and normalization bound essential tori using mod-2 homology.
still_required_locally: Knot-exterior irreducibility and peripheral incompressibility bridge.
Full local proof of required Seifert classification prerequisites.
Separate hyperbolization theorem for atoroidal pieces.

exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.locator: The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds, Ch. 5 §5.8, Theorem 5.8.2, PDF p. 22 / printed p. 104.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.hypotheses: Complete finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold with finitely many torus cusps.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.claim: A neighborhood of infinity in the product surgery-parameter space gives fillings with hyperbolic structures; primitive integral slopes there are smooth hyperbolic fillings.
proof_ingredients: Local deformation family of dimension equal to number of cusps.
still_required_locally: Mostow rigidity and analytic openness proofs or complete verified suppliers.
Do not infer hyperbolicity from atoroidality.

exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.locator: Hass-Lagarias-Pippenger, Theorems 5.4, 5.6 and 8.1; PDF pp. 13, 14 and 22.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.hypotheses: Finite PL knot diagram with n crossings; good triangulation of compact exterior with t=O(n) tetrahedra.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.claim: Finite Haken search O(exp(c n²)) time/O(n² log n) space; JT vertex search O(exp(c' n)) time/same space; NP certificate.
proof_ingredients: Disk topology and nonzero mod-2 meridian intersection verification.
still_required_locally: Normal form theorem proof; finite coordinate bounds; vertex theorem proof; disk/unknot proof via longitude kernel and PL Schoenflies; explicit Turing model and bit-complexity proof.

exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.locator: NYJM 30 (2024), Theorem 4.1, journal p. 578 / PDF p. 18; Theorem 5.2 at ideal points.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.hypotheses: Admissible representation on an irreducible character component with one-dimensional image under peripheral restriction.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.claim: s_K = -(M/L)(∂_M A/∂_L A) in paper's variable order A(L,M); at an ideal point slope is minus the associated Culler-Shalen boundary / Newton edge slope.
proof_ingredients: Adjoint twisted-homology kernel as Lagrangian/conormal data.
Logarithmic local coordinates and chain rule.
still_required_locally: Complete Culler-Shalen surface theorem, unless separately imported with exact contract.

exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.theorem: Baldwin-Sivek enhanced A-polynomial / SL(2,C)-abelian surgery classification
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.locator: Mathematische Annalen 394 (2026), Theorems 1.1, 1.2; accepted preprint v2 28 Nov 2025.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.hypotheses: Knot K in S3; rational surgery slopes; enhanced polynomial defined from irreducible representation locus.
exact_contracts_and_proof_modules.claim: Infinitely many SL(2,C)-abelian surgeries iff torus knot; enhanced Newton polygon thin iff torus knot.
proof_ingredients: Alexander polynomial constraints exclude satellite knots.
Hyperbolic Dehn filling / faithful representation excludes hyperbolic case.
